questions.title: OLS PRESS leave-one-out residual identity
questions.description: Focused L0 known-result evaluation grounded in Allen (1974) and the declared statsmodels OLSInfluence convention. Let X be a finite real n by p design matrix used exactly as supplied, with n>p, full column rank, and every delete-one design X_{-i} still full column rank. Let y be a finite n-vector, beta_hat=(X'X)^{-1}X'y, H=X(X'X)^{-1}X', h_i=H_ii, fitted=X beta_hat, and e=y-fitted. In one authoritative Markdown/LaTeX theory workspace, derive the exact coefficient downdate beta_hat_{-i}=beta_hat-(X'X)^{-1}x_i e_i/(1-h_i) using a valid rank-one inverse argument. Deduce that the prediction residual for observation i from the model fitted without i is e_i/(1-h_i), and hence PRESS=sum_i (e_i/(1-h_i))^2. Prove why delete-one full rank is equivalent to 1-h_i>0 under the stated assumptions, distinguish PRESS residuals from ordinary and studentized residuals, and establish normal-equation consistency, row-permutation equivariance, invariance of fitted values, residuals, leverage, leave-one-out residuals, and PRESS under any invertible change of design-column basis, and the declared outcome-scaling law. Do not use numerical agreement as proof. The required model-authored artifact is est_ols_press and must implement the frozen Python run_estimator(request) contract exactly, without adding an intercept or coercing malformed values. Exploratory Python or R may compare the shortcut with explicit delete-one refits. A separately frozen confirmatory assessment uses predeclared random full-rank designs and outcomes, compares every returned quantity with independent linear algebra and brute-force refits, and records numerical error under fixed tolerances. That is computational validation, not proof of the universal identity. Source-code replication, novelty, and Lean formalization are not applicable.

primary_paper.title: The Relationship Between Variable Selection and Data Augmentation and a Method for Prediction

implementation_convention.title: statsmodels OLSInfluence resid_press and ess_press
implementation_convention.meaning: The public implementation computes PRESS residuals as ordinary OLS residuals divided by one minus the hat diagonal and sums their squares; the task contract below is the executable authority.

request_fields.name: design
request_fields.meaning: The real design matrix X used exactly as supplied; an intercept is present only if explicitly included as a column.
request_fields.shape: n nonempty rows of a common positive length p with n>p, full column rank, and every delete-one design full column rank
request_fields.indexing: rows are observations and columns are regressors
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, strings, nonfinite values, empty or ragged arrays, n<=p, rank deficiency, or any delete-one rank deficiency; do not coerce or add an intercept.

request_fields.name: outcome
request_fields.meaning: The finite real response vector y aligned with the rows of design.
request_fields.indexing: entry i corresponds to design row i
request_fields.edge_cases: Reject booleans, strings, nonfinite values, nested values, or any length other than n; do not coerce.

response_fields.name: coefficients
response_fields.meaning: The full-data ordinary least-squares coefficient vector beta_hat.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must solve the supplied full-rank least-squares problem without an implicit intercept.
response_fields.normalization: (X'X)^{-1}X'y, evaluated by a numerically stable equivalent solver

response_fields.name: fitted
response_fields.meaning: The full-data fitted values X beta_hat.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must equal design times coefficients under the supplied column convention.

response_fields.name: residuals
response_fields.meaning: The ordinary full-data residuals e=y-X beta_hat.
response_fields.edge_cases: These are ordinary residuals, not studentized or delete-one residuals.

response_fields.name: leverage
response_fields.meaning: The diagonal h_i of the full-data OLS hat matrix H.
response_fields.shape: exactly n finite real scalars strictly below one and at least zero up to numerical tolerance
response_fields.edge_cases: Each one-minus-leverage denominator must be strictly positive under the admitted domain.

response_fields.name: loo_residuals
response_fields.meaning: The leave-one-out prediction residual y_i-x_i' beta_hat_{-i} for every observation.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must be the exact delete-one residual, not the ordinary or studentized residual.

response_fields.name: press
response_fields.meaning: The predicted residual error sum of squares.
response_fields.edge_cases: Must sum squared leave-one-out residuals without averaging or studentization.

invariants.meaning: The request contains exactly design and outcome, and the response contains exactly coefficients, fitted, residuals, leverage, loo_residuals, and press. Missing, extra, malformed, nonfinite, or coercible-only values are rejected.

The full-data outputs satisfy fitted=X coefficients, residuals=outcome-fitted, X' residuals=0 up to numerical tolerance, leverage=diag(H), every loo_residual equals both residual/(1-leverage) and the residual from an explicit delete-one refit, and press is their squared sum.
Applying the same row permutation to design and outcome leaves coefficients and press unchanged and applies that permutation to fitted, residuals, leverage, and loo_residuals.
For any invertible p by p matrix A, replacing design X by X A transforms coefficients to A^{-1} coefficients while fitted, residuals, leverage, loo_residuals, and press remain unchanged.
Multiplying outcome by a finite nonzero scalar c multiplies coefficients, fitted, residuals, and loo_residuals by c, leaves leverage unchanged, and multiplies press by c^2.

empirical_claims.meaning: Every frozen scenario fixes dimensions, design generator, outcome generator, seed, replicate count, and tolerances before candidate execution and invokes the accepted estimator through the exact public request.
Candidate coefficients, fitted values, ordinary residuals, leverage, and PRESS agree with an independent stable full-data least-squares and hat-diagonal implementation under frozen tolerances.
Every candidate leave-one-out residual agrees with a separately fitted delete-one least-squares model for the corresponding observation under frozen tolerances.
Finite random-design agreement is numerical validation only and does not prove the universal rank-one identity or its domain conditions.
